page: Microsoft Azure E4-2s_v6 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Esv6 server family. It features 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical Intel Xeon 8573C core running at 4.2 GHz with hyper-threading enabled. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-core ratio of 16.0 GB per core. It does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, but it is Premium Storage capable.

Benchmark results show a divergence between single-core and multi-core performance. The single-core Geekbench score is strong at 2146.0, and single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression perform at average levels. However, multi-core benchmarks are limited by the 2-vCPU configuration, with stress-ng multi-core performance and Geekbench multi-core scores categorized as poor and weak respectively. Memory bandwidth tests also show weak to poor performance, with large-block read-only bandwidth at 21.51 GB/sec and write bandwidth at 14.37 GB/sec.

Given the high memory allocation relative to the limited compute capacity, this server is configured for memory-bound workloads that do not require high parallel processing power. It is suitable for small-scale database operations, caching layers, and lightweight text processing. The lack of local storage and weak multi-threaded performance represent clear tradeoffs, making it less suitable for intensive compilation, ray tracing, or large-scale LLM inference. Qualitatively, it offers high memory density per vCPU, providing a cost-efficient option for memory-heavy applications that would otherwise require provisioning larger, more expensive compute instances.
